html:
Vladimir Lenin was a Russian revolutionary who led the Bolshevik party to power in the October Revolution of 1917 and founded the Soviet state. He ruled it until his death in 1924 through a one party dictatorship backed by the secret police and the Red Terror.

He was born Vladimir Ulyanov in Simbirsk on the Volga, son of a school inspector. In 1887 his older brother was hanged for plotting to kill the tsar. Lenin turned to the ideas of Karl Marx, was exiled to Siberia, and spent most of 1900 to 1917 abroad, in Munich, London, Geneva and Zurich.

His key idea was a tightly organised party of professional revolutionaries to lead the workers. Over this, Russia's Marxists split in 1903 into his Bolsheviks and the Mensheviks.

1917 and after:

  • The February Revolution toppled the tsar while Lenin was in Zurich. The German government let him travel home in a sealed train, hoping he would take Russia out of the war.
  • In October (November in the new calendar) the Bolsheviks seized power in Petrograd, the Russian Revolution.
  • He dissolved the elected Constituent Assembly, made peace with Germany at Brest-Litovsk in 1918 at the cost of huge lands, and won the civil war that followed.
  • Grain was seized by force; famine followed in 1921. He then allowed some private trade, the New Economic Policy.
  • The Soviet Union, the state the chart traces in Muscovy, Russia, USSR, was formed in 1922.

He was weakened by an assassin's bullets in 1918 and then strokes. In his last notes he warned against Stalin, who nonetheless succeeded him. His body was embalmed and still lies in a mausoleum on Red Square.
